subject: DPA redlines: roles, routing and export controls
messages:
From: Dana Saito <dana.saito@pulseops.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@pulseops.com
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: PulseOps DPA redline (first pass)

Hi Mateo,

Attached is our first-pass redline to the proposed DPA and the SCCs you sent last week (PulseOps_DPA_Redline_v2.docx). Key points we flagged up front:

- Controller/Processor ambiguity in Section 2 — we need clarity on whether PulseOps will be controller for analytics telemetry.
- Hosting region language references "EU or US" — procurement requires an explicit default of EU for EU customer data, with US only by exception.
- KMS/Key control: we prefer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) where possible; please confirm if Redwood supports KMS integration or HSM options for dedicated/private deployments.
- Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) — can Redwood provide a short summary of technical mitigations used for transfers? Your SCC cover letter is helpful but we need explicit steps.
- Subprocessor list and onboarding cadence — procurement wants a committed monthly update cadence and a named POC.

Suggest a 30-min sync next week to walk through the redline; can you confirm availability?

Thanks,
Dana Saito
Senior Counsel, PulseOps
Dana.Saito@pulseops.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachment: PulseOps_DPA_Redline_v2.docx (word/docx, 142 KB)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Dana Saito <dana.saito@pulseops.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PulseOps DPA redline (first pass)

Dana — thanks for the detailed pass and the redline. We reviewed internally and want to align before a call. Quick answers up front:

- Controller/Processor: Redwood is the processor for inference and hosting; we can add clarifying language that PulseOps is controller for customer-provided data and for telemetry used for their analytics. We will propose explicit definitions and a short examples table.
- Hosting region default: we can set EU default for EU customer data and specify an exception flow that requires written approval; will capture in Order Form as a region selector (orderform param).
- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted API supports envelope encryption with customer KMS for enterprise tiers. We'll list supported KMS providers and HSM options in the DPA exhibit.
- TIA: we'll provide a 2-page Transfer Impact Addendum summary and link to technical mitigations (prefix/KV caching constraints, egress controls, subnet routing).
- Subprocessor cadence: propose monthly list with a 15-business-day notice for new subprocessors and a named Redwood ops POC (Ben Carter).

Can we do Tue 11/10 09:00 PT for a 30-min call? If that works, I'll send the calendar invite and a consolidated tracked-change doc.

Mateo Alvarez
Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Mobile: (650) 555-0122

Attachment: Redwood_Response_DPA_v1.docx (contains proposed tracked changes)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: PulseOps redline - paper notes and recommended language

Quick internal notes / suggested language (high level):

1) Definitions (Section 1) — add: "Controller: the party that determines the purpose and means of processing customer data; Processor: Redwood Inference when acting to host, serve, or infer models per Order Form."

2) Clause: Hosting region and routing (new subclause) — propose: "Customer may select primary hosting region in the Order Form. For EU customer data, Redwood will by default serve from EU-hosted capacity unless Customer authorizes transfer in writing. Any fallback to non-EU routing will be subject to the Transfer Impact Addendum and documented in the Order Form."

3) KMS/HSM (security exhibit) — options table: Hosted (envelope encryption) / Dedicated (BYOK via AWS KMS, GCP KMS) / Private (HSM integration). Add a one-sentence escalation path for security exceptions and an SLA for key-rotation support (business-hours response).

4) SCCs & TIA — we should attach our standard TIA summary and ask them to confirm equivalence to their internal assessment. For any non-EU hosting we must spell out technical mitigations (e.g., dedicated subnets, egress block lists, contractually-scoped customer data subsets).

5) Subprocessors — accept monthly cadence; propose: Redwood will provide a rolling 30-day posted list and 15-business-day notice for material new subprocessors. POC: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.com).

6) Order Form tie-ins — call out an explicit Order Form exhibit that captures region selector, BYOK option, and any pricing impact for dedicated EU-resident pools. Point Laura for pricing impact modeling.

Action: Mateo to consolidate and return a single tracked-change document; Laura to provide estimated delta for EU-resident dedicated pool fee.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

(Internal only)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Consolidated responses + proposed edits (next steps)

Dana — following our internal review, please find the consolidated response below and a link to a single tracked-change file in Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AbCdeDPA (Drive: DPA consolidated). We also attached a cleaned Order Form with region selector and a short TIA summary. Highlighted items for your team:

1) Controller/Processor: Confirmed language added to Section 2. Example table included (analytics telemetry = controlled by PulseOps unless explicitly opted into Redwood product analytics).
2) Hosting region default: Order Form now contains a "Primary Hosting Region" field. For EU customer data, primary = EU unless Customer selects otherwise and signs the transfer exception addendum.
3) KMS/HSM: Options table added in Security Exhibit (BYOK supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted API supports envelope + customer KMS integration for enterprise). Please indicate your preferred KMS provider if you want us to pre-authorize in the Order Form.
4) TIA: attached 2-page Transfer Impact Addendum summary; includes routing/egress controls, subnet isolation, and prefix handling.
4a) SCCs: we are asking to execute the latest EU SCCs + the TIA as an exhibit; Redwood proposes an administrative acceptance of SCCs with a 30-day review period for any material changes.
5) Subprocessor cadence: Redwood agrees to monthly posted lists and 15-business-day notice for new material subprocessors. Ben Carter is the ops POC (ben_carter@redwood.com).

Attachments: Redwood_Response_DPA_v1.docx (tracked changes), OrderForm_PulseOps_v3.pdf, Drive link above.

Next steps we propose:
- Please confirm any redlines you expect to retain by EOD 11/13 so we can route to exec approvals.
- If acceptable, we will send an Order Form + DPA bundle via DocuSign for signature and include a line item for EU-resident dedicated pool pricing (Laura to insert).
- If you prefer, we can run a 30-min technical handoff for your security team to walk the TIA — we can schedule for the week of 11/16.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week.

Mateo Alvarez
Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
(650) 555-0122

Mateo — thanks for the crisp consolidation and the Drive link. Quick replies:

- Controller/Processor language looks good to our counsel; we will keep a very small telemetry carveout but will accept your example table as a starting point.
- Region selector and Order Form language: procurement approves the EU-default + exception flow. Please add a one-line definition of "EU customer data" to the Order Form exhibit (we will share a suggested definition).
- KMS: PulseOps will want BYOK for our production EU dataset (we are standardizing on AWS KMS). Please include pre-authorized KMS scope in the Order Form.
- TIA: security team reviewed the 2-page summary and would like a 30-min technical sync on 11/18 or 11/19. Can Ben and Karthik join?
- Subprocessors cadence: procurement approves monthly posting.

We are ready to take the final DPA + Order Form to our C-suite for sign-off once the KMS line and the small telemetry carveout language are in place. Please send the DocuSign bundle when ready; procurement will circulate the PO after countersignature.

Thanks — Dana
